spec.name: Reversal v30
spec.notes: Fade the last move, rebalanced often.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.0, annual return 7%, maximum drawdown 5%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.98 to -1.31 (change -3.29).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.98 to 1.98. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is -0.43 (as submitted, 2 bps: 1.98); it breaks even at 8.6 bps with daily turnover 0.45.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.98 against 1.98 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is -1.01 against 1.98 in research, a gap of +2.99.
The best year gives 28% of total P&L (year 1) and calm regimes give 67%; Sharpe is 2.19 in calm and 1.82 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 5 distinct specs; the best of 5 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.27, so the claimed 2.00 becomes 1.73 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.58 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.05, 95th percentile 0.45).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.98 to as low as 1.74 (as low as 1.74 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 40% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 25% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
